topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory welcome and sets the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy along with their toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular defects and hormone dependencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair, are exploited therapeutically.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic drivers and kinase inhibitor therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the inhibition of oncogenic kinase drivers, the molecular mechanics of kinase inhibitors, and the evolution of bypass resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates target specific cell-surface antigens to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and methods to harness T cells through checkpoint inhibition, bispecific engagers, and CAR-T cell therapy.

topics.label: Challenges, historical perspectives, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the ongoing challenges, historical shifts in mortality and prevention, and emerging paradigms in personalized cancer care.
